source.title: LlmFixer: Fix the Helpfulness of Defensive Large Language Models
source.authors: Ze-Long Yu; Xiao-Ming Zhang; Li-Tian Zhang; Yuan-Yuan Yuan; Chao-Zhuo Li

record.tranche_reason: The study applies GCG jailbreak attacks and reports attack success rates, which test whether adversarial suffix attacks can bypass safety. It does not test the fine-tuning or first-token mechanisms in the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: GCG attack success rates are recorded for V4. The benign-prompt false-reject and quality results evaluate helpfulness, not whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance; the study does not measure token-position KL or safety localization. Other attack columns are not included as rows for V4 because they are not identified as suffix attacks in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes LlmFixer, a prompt re-writer plus logic patch meant to restore helpfulness to defended LLMs. Jailbreak attacks (GCG, PAIR, AutoDAN, SAP30, DeepInception) serve only as a safety check on the authors' own method, so ASR is reported to show LlmFixer does not raise it. The study does not ask whether suffixes, prefills or decoding changes defeat refusal, and gives no GCG setup (suffix length, per-model optimization). It has no fine-tuning-induced harm, no token-position KL, no localization analysis and no deepening training. Its undefended-model GCG rates (Llama3 8%, Qwen 22%, Vicuna 62%) are baselines for its own method, not a test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that LlmFixer recovers the helpfulness of defended LLMs (lower FRR, generally higher quality) while preserving safety. They report that it rarely increases ASR and sometimes reduces it.
record.recipe_differences: The claim concerns fine-tuning safety-trained chat models on small harmful or benign datasets and token-position safety effects. This study trains a prompt re-writer using reinforcement learning and trains an added logic patch; it evaluates GCG and other jailbreak attacks against defended models.
record.method_sensitivity: GCG ASR varies by model, defense, LlmFixer configuration and model size; the study reports different rates across these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: An added FFN-side logic patch and an RL-trained prompt re-writer lower false-reject rates on vaguely benign prompts. GCG/PAIR/AutoDAN/SAP/DeepInception ASR stays roughly unchanged or slightly lower, though it rises in a few cells (e.g., Llama3 GCG 8% to 10%, ICD DeepInception 0% to 5%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Helpfulness-recovery add-ons on defended LLMs can reduce over-refusal without materially raising jailbreak ASR.

record.code_released: The code and data are stated to be submitted as supplementary materials and publicly available upon publication; URL not stated.
record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR results. The authors note that robustness against sophisticated, multi-step adversarial attacks remains uncertain; the reported attack evaluation is limited to the tested attacks and settings.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Left out GCG-ASR results in Table 3 (Vicuna component ablation), Appendix A.2/Table 5 (rewriter-model comparisons), and Appendix A.3/Table 6 (transfer comparison), plus the Figure 3 statement that parameter changes did not affect ASR. These additional attack-rate comparisons were omitted after retaining the main results, the model-size comparison and Appendix A.1 component-ablation results.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of the target model.
No benign fine-tuning of the target model. The logic patch and re-writer are trained, but harmful compliance after benign training is not framed as safety erosion.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling or decoding-change bypass. GCG is used only as an evaluation attack, with no study of the opening tokens.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels should be dropped. 'challenges' for 0% ASR under defenses is wrong: V4 does not predict that GCG succeeds against added defenses. The defended and ablation rows compare the study's own method and are not tests of the claim. The undefended GCG baselines (Llama3-8B 8%, Qwen2.5-7B 22%, Vicuna-7B 62%) could at most be weak context for V4, but no attack configuration is given. The paper cites Qi et al. 2024 (an original source) only for the HEx-PHI dataset.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning with harmful examples and its effect on compliance.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data and harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence by response position on harmful prompts.
Tests GCG attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes as bypass interventions.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether the data or training objective causes safety shallowness.
Training safety across more response tokens and its robustness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GCG on unprotected Vicuna, with and without LlmFixer
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASR is 62% and 52%, respectively, showing substantial GCG success in these conditions (R21–R22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GCG conditions with a nonzero ASR below 62%
reader_labels.reason: GCG succeeds in some cases, but the reported rates are incomplete and vary by model, defense and configuration (R01–R02, R09–R10, R11–R12, R15–R16, R18–R20, R23–R30, R44–R48, R51–R60).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: No GCG successes are reported in these tested settings, including several defended models and ablation conditions (R03–R08, R13–R14, R17, R31–R43, R50).
